cases.statement: Two people from one Japanese family: a hemizygous affected son (II-2) and his heterozygous affected mother (I-2) (29463847). The son is also Family 16's proband in the 30413001 survey (merged by the pipeline; 30413001 cites 29463847 as reference [19] for Family 16).

people.label: II-2
people.key_phenotypes: hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; muscle weakness; mild intellectual disability; liver dysfunction; autophagic vacuoles on muscle biopsy; no cerebral artery stenosis

quotes.quote: The affected son (II-2) was hemizygous for c.1009_1010 delGT: p.Val337Phe fs*12 (delGT), while the mother (I-2) was heterozygous.
Her 16-year-old son (II-2) sought medical attention for muscle weakness, liver dysfunction, and mild intellectual disability.
Muscle biopsy demonstrated numerous AV among the myofibrils (Supplementary Fig. S6).
He had HCM similar to that in his mother, but he lacked any stenosis of the cerebral arteries (Supplementary Fig. S1b).

people.label: I-2
people.key_phenotypes: ischemic stroke at 47 with diffuse narrowing of the cerebral arteries; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy; no skeletal muscle, intellectual or liver abnormality

quotes.quote: The affected son (II-2) was hemizygous for c.1009_1010 delGT: p.Val337Phe fs*12 (delGT), while the mother (I-2) was heterozygous.
In the first family, a 50-year-old female (I-2) (Fig. 1a) developed ischemic stroke with transient left hemiparesis at the age of 47, which was successfully treated by by-pass surgery.
Cardiac imaging studies revealed hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) but no intracardiac thrombus (Supplementary Fig. S5a).
She had no abnormalities in skeletal muscle function, intellectual ability, and liver functions.

phenotype_specificity.statement: The son's combination of HCM, myopathy with autophagic vacuoles, intellectual disability and liver dysfunction is described by the authors as typical full-blown Danon disease; the mother had cardiomyopathy and young-onset stroke without atherosclerotic risk factors. Testing of other genes is not reported.

quotes.quote: The male proband had a hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy, intellectual disability, and liver functions, consistent with the diagnosis of a typical full‐blown Danon disease.

She did not have any clinical risk factors for atherosclerosis, including hypertension, smoking, or dyslipidemia, nor was there any obvious stenosis in the aorta or its branches (Supplementary Fig. S4).
These clinical features raised the possibility of Danon disease.

segregation.statement: Two affected carriers in one family: affected hemizygous son and affected heterozygous mother. No other relatives are reported as tested; 30413001 Table 1 lists the same two affected people (proband and mother) for Family 16.

quotes.quote: Sequence analysis of the LAMP2 gene (NM_013995.2) disclosed that the mother is heterozygous for a novel frameshift mutation (c.1009_1010 delGT), while her affected son is hemizygous (Fig. 1a).

de_novo.statement: Not de novo in the son: his mother carries the variant. Testing of the mother's parents is not reported.

quotes.quote: Sequence analysis of the LAMP2 gene (NM_013995.2) disclosed that the mother is heterozygous for a novel frameshift mutation (c.1009_1010 delGT), while her affected son is hemizygous (Fig. 1a).

functional.statement: Patient tissue: Western blot of the son's skeletal muscle showed only trace LAMP-2 (truncated protein barely expressed) versus abundant expression in control muscle. No construct assay.

quotes.quote: Western analysis with a skeletal muscle biopsy specimen from the affected son revealed that the truncated LAMP-2 protein was barely expressed (Fig. 1d).
LAMP-2 is abundantly expressed in control muscle, whereas only trace levels were found in the patient’s muscle.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Two-base deletion predicted to cause a frameshift (p.(Val337PhefsTer12)). The authors state it is predicted to delete the C-terminal transmembrane domain encoded by exon 9, the lysosomal targeting signal.

quotes.quote: This mutation is predicted to delete the C-terminal transmembrane spanning domain of the LAMP-2 protein encoded by the last coding exon 9, which serves as the lysosomal targeting signal.
These disease variants are predicted to lose a proper membrane anchoring (family 1) or protein folding (family 2), thereby causing a functional LAMP‐2 deficiency.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Cohort-level statement in 30413001: none of the survey's mutations was found in 100 Japanese controls.

quotes.quote: On screening 100 Japanese controls, the same mutations were not found.

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it a novel frameshift mutation and state that the molecular studies confirmed Danon disease in this family; no formal classification is given.

quotes.quote: Sequence analysis of the LAMP2 gene (NM_013995.2) disclosed that the mother is heterozygous for a novel frameshift mutation (c.1009_1010 delGT), while her affected son is hemizygous (Fig. 1a).
These molecular studies confirmed the diagnosis of Danon disease in this family.

concerns: 29463847 names transcript NM_013995.2, not the batch's NM_002294.3. The two papers agree on c.1009_1010delGT and 29463847 says it lies upstream of exon 9, but the panel should confirm the coordinate maps the same on both transcripts.
The mother is labelled I-2 in the main text and Figure 1 legend but '(I‐1)' in Supplementary Table S1 of 29463847.

Same-person link: 30413001 Family 16 (reference [19] = 29463847) is this family; the pipeline merged the son (DANON-ID0071). 30413001's female patient with young-onset stroke from diffuse cerebral artery narrowing is very likely mother I-2, but the survey does not name her family.

30413001 contradicts itself on recurrent variants: the text says Family 11 and Family 15 share c.877C > T, while Table 1 lists c.877C>T for Families 10 and 14, c.371_372 delCA for Family 11 and c.56T>C for Family 15.
30413001 gives two different counts for families whose mothers or relatives tested negative (eight families in Results, 10 families in Discussion) and does not say which families these are.
notes_for_panel: Both carriers are affected; the son has residual trace LAMP-2 on Western blot. No unaffected relatives are described.
